.art & animation

Ride the artmaking cycle

I used to want to work for Disney. Then I moved to NYC and found myself working as an animator and storyboard artist on PBS’s WordWorld. Somewhere along the way, I became frustrated with what I thought was the monotony of the work—only to realize, years later, that it wasn’t monotony at all. It was me bumping up against the limitations of my own craft. All of this is to say: uncovering your personal approach to the creative process is a lifelong journey. I’m deeply grateful to still be on it.

Those who continue to make art are those who...have learned not to quit.

Below you'll find various output of my artistic endeavors—enjoy!

Subaqueous

It’s not often that I get to combine my visual and musical work. This piece is an experimental exploration of both, featuring music recorded on a Roland Juno-60 and Fender Rhodes, with visuals driven by audio-spectrum experiments in Adobe After Effects. I made a conscious effort not to plan, overanalyze, or perfect the outcome—a mindset I don’t practice often enough. Here’s to more play and less purpose.

Lythoos

This piece began as improvisational music recorded on a Juno-60 synthesizer. Individual tracks were exported and used to drive audio-spectrum visualizations in Adobe After Effects.

Nah Talk Pon Phone

I had a great time creating a lyric video for reggae artist Uzimon. In Nah Talk Pon Phone, he humorously shares his preference for texting over phone calls—text first, so he can decide if it’s worth the chat. The video was created using After Effects, Sketch, Premiere, and Photoshop.

Sleep Video Test

During the development of this lyric video, I explored an illustrated world for the character to exist within. This short clip captures an early test of color-keying a live-action element over custom illustrated background elements.

Loop for Soho Playhouse

The artist requested something zany and silly to loop at any point during their live performance. This motion graphic was created in a single afternoon. The music was added afterward and was not used during the live show—it’s an original composition written and recorded by me on a Juno-60.
